question.text: Under the default (new) tax regime per Section 115BAC(1A), the surcharge cap applicable to a trust taxed at MMR is:

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states: 'Under this new regime [115BAC(1A)], the rate of surcharge shall be capped at 25% (instead of 37%).' Hence the default MMR stack is 30% base + 25% surcharge + 4% health-and-education cess = 39% effective, versus 42.744% under the old 37% surcharge cap (30 × 1.37 × 1.04). The Trap: 37% was the old-regime peak surcharge (still cited in the workbook's 42.744% MMR). 15% is the special LTCG/STCG surcharge cap under Section 112A/111A. 10% is a lower surcharge slab. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D (Cat I/II) rarely hits MMR because of pass-through. XIX-C/XIX-E drill the surcharge-cap nuance because Cat III pays at fund level. Individual-tax exams (XXI-A, X-A) test the same cap at investor level. Manager's Pro-Tip: When CFOs at Cat III funds model tax drag, default to the 25% surcharge cap unless the trust opts OUT of Section 115BAC(1A). For LTCG/STCG, remember the EVEN LOWER 15% surcharge cap applies — building this into the NAV accrual model prevents over-provisioning and NAV dilution.
